International News · 16 Sources · 4 Regions

Daily Brief

G7 foreign ministers convened in Paris on Monday with Secretary of State Marco Rubio facing pressure from European allies over the Iran war and Ukraine negotiations, days after Republicans suffered major midterm losses widely attributed to the unpopularity of the conflict [RFI, France 24, Le Monde]. The meeting precedes US-Russia-Ukraine talks scheduled for Tuesday in Abu Dhabi. In Poland, the suspect in Saturday's Krakow mass shooting that killed nine people—including six in the city center and three family members—died in hospital, as authorities continued investigating potential far-right motivations while politicians debated the gunman's ideology [BBC, ABC Australia]. COP31 opened in Antalya, Turkey, with US delegates attending but not participating in negotiations, as nations remain divided over fossil fuel commitments and climate finance for developing countries [RFI]. In South Africa, local election results showed the ANC falling to under 32% of the national vote, marking a historic decline for the party that has governed since 1994 [The Guardian]. Meanwhile, at least 13 migrants drowned off the coast of Crete as Mediterranean crossings continue to surge past 2025 levels [BBC, Le Monde].

Krakow Mass Shooting Suspect Dies as Poland Debates Gunman's Far-Right Links

  • The 24-year-old Polish gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square and three family members at his home died in hospital on Monday

COP31 Opens in Turkey with US Observers Only as Nations Remain Divided on Fossil Fuels

  • UN climate talks began Monday in Antalya, Turkey, running until November 20 under a joint Turkish-Australian arrangement
  • US delegates will attend but not participate in negotiations, following the Trump administration's climate policy shifts
  • UNEP warned in October that existing policies could drive warming to 2.8°C this century, with a sustained breach of 1.5°C now considered unavoidable
  • Poorer nations are pressing for climate finance to address floods and droughts while fossil fuel commitments remain contentious

04 Geopolitics

ANC Falls Below 32% in South African Local Elections, Marking Historic Decline

  • The ANC received 31.8% of the national vote with over 80% of ballots counted, down nearly 14 points from 2021
  • The party is projected to lose its position as the largest party in Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa's two most populous provinces
  • The Democratic Alliance received 24.1% and Jacob Zuma's MK party received 9.3%
  • Voter turnout increased to approximately 54.5%, up from 46% in the previous local elections

At Least 13 Migrants Drown Off Crete as Mediterranean Crossings Surge

  • Thirteen Sudanese nationals died when their boat sank approximately 15 nautical miles off the coast of Crete
  • Eighteen survivors were rescued, with four including a toddler taken to hospital
  • Authorities believe the boat had been at sea for days and struggled to reach shore due to strong winds
